governing_spec.section: Section B: Journal Consumer Isolation & Old-Writer Retirement

transactional_cas_writes.implementation: services/governance/decision_journal.py: Atomic multi-store transaction with bundle file locking and crash recovery bound strictly to durable transaction identity (_tx_id, scoped idempotency_key, tenant, actor, user, request, and entry). Reservation is registered in idempotency store with status pending. Entry CAS commits atomically first with durable transaction history and before-entry snapshot, followed by secondary store commit (outbox and audit), after which idempotency is finalized with status succeeded. Readers and subsequent writers coordinate reads and recovery with live writer transaction outcome. While a writer holds bundle lock, readers read committed before-entry state, and concurrent retries return pending without falsely finalizing or replaying uncommitted CAS writes that subsequently roll back. Fabricated-data version/title and raw-key success fallbacks removed; crash recovery never finalizes with failed secondary writes.

append_only_audit_with_diff.implementation: services/governance/decision_journal.py: patch_entry computes changedFields, diff changes (before/after) and appends audit record bound to actor_id, user_id, and tenant_id. list_audit_events strictly enforces tenant scope and authorized principal on audit reads: omitted or blank tenant denies tenant-scoped events; private entry diffs are denied unless queried by matching actor/user.

durable_outbox_streaming.implementation: services/governance/decision_journal.py: outbox record store initialized and populated on entry creation and updates with decision_journal.entry.* event types with explicit tenant_id, actor_id, and user_id scoping. Creation includes its idempotency and outbox in recoverable commit: fresh-process retries after creation crash recover and emit the creation outbox event.

tenant_and_user_isolation.implementation: services/governance/decision_journal.py: Unified fail-closed _is_entry_accessible policy across get_entry, list_entries, DecisionJournalOwnerAdapter detail/list, DomainDecisionJournalReaderPort detail/list, and InMemoryOperationsConsultationPort. Tenant-scoped records strictly require matching tenant; tenant-only queries without actor deny private records; unscoped queries deny tenant-scoped records; legacy records missing tenant require explicit include_unscoped_legacy=True (ordinary unscoped reads denied even for authored legacy); and private records require matching authorized principal (actor_id/user_id). Recovery and replay strictly recheck result access so crashed unauthorized reservations never replay other principals' private entries.

caller_supplied_id_collision_rejection.implementation: services/governance/decision_journal.py: create_entry raises DecisionJournalCollisionError when a supplied ID collides with another principal's or tenant's record. AgoraService binds create replay durably to principal and request hash, surviving new service instances.

controlled_legacy_migration.implementation: services/governance/migrations/journal_migration.py: JournalMigrationEngine verifies principal ownership (createdBy/actor_id/userId) and SHA-256 checksum parity before destination mutation or disposition. Unscoped destination collisions with mismatched author or content are strictly rejected as conflicts. Requires or recovers checksum/principal-bound durable migration audit before every disposal path, including skipped_identical and checkpoint resume; source is strictly preserved on missing proof.

unscoped_legacy_isolation.implementation: Ordinary unscoped reads (include_unscoped_legacy=False) fail closed on legacy rows missing tenant_id even if authored by caller; governed legacy access (include_unscoped_legacy=True) required. Ordinary patch strictly requires clean_tenant and fails closed on unscoped legacy rows pending governed migration; missing scope matrix verified across all readers and adapters.

fresh_process_restart_parity.implementation: CoordinatingJsonGovernanceRecordStore uses POSIX file locking (fcntl.flock) and cache invalidation on get/list_all/put/insert_if_absent/compare_and_set/delete to guarantee that multiple long-lived store instances across processes and threads coordinate safely without cache clobbering or losing committed records.
